report: Checked the three candidate lemmas. הוּא: three suffixes (us, his, him) each take the pronoun written for them under rule 18; the difference is the ASV's, not a split. הָלַל: v.1 'Oh praise' keeps the volitive 'Oh' with the verb (rule 17) and its 'ye' goes to the vocative noun it stands before ('all ye nations', rule 36's position test, as 'all ye stars of light'); v.2 'Praise ye Jehovah' has no vocative and the 'ye' stands after the imperative, so it is the verb's subject pronoun (rule 17). Both verses follow the same rule and differ only because the English puts the pronoun in different places. יהוה: bare 'Jehovah' as object/subject versus 'of Jehovah' as nomen rectum (rule 19) — licensed by the construct chain.

The one BSB disagreement (v.1 article הָ before אֻמִּים, ASV unrepresented) is the documented rule 36 convention: the ASV writes no 'the' for the vocative and the 'ye' belongs to the noun, not the article. Not an error.

v.2 'endureth for ever' on the predicate לְ follows the contract's own example לְעוֹלָם חַסְדּוֹ (rules 20 and 49); 'is great' on גָּבַר heads on the complement under rule 44. Both notes name the competing reading.
No chapter-wide judgment beyond what the contract already states; no convention or promotion warranted.
